title: Нагиев присоединяется к ужину  (Nagiyev Joins the Late Dinner)

segments.t: Just as Chef Barinov is about to lose his temper at Vika and her waitresses for tricking the kitchen into cooking their staff dinner, Nagiyev strolls into the dining room. Forced to smile and play along, Viktor Petrovich watches helplessly as Nagiyev sits down and orders another salad.
А что это мы хомячим, а?
Надеюсь, не за мой счет, а?
Ладно, давайте мне тоже вот там бы накрыть.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Let me call you back in a minute.' Max addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'will call back'. Kostya answers right away.
'Where did I just walk in, a zoo?' Kostya anchors the line on 'where', while 'came' completes the thought.
А что это мы хомячим, а?
'And what are we all munching on here, huh?' Max brings out the contrast between 'and' and 'what' in a few short words.
Надеюсь, не за мой счет, а?
'Not on my tab, I hope, huh?' The grammar packs 'hope so' and 'and' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Max answers right away.
'No, no, of course not.' In Russian, the idea of 'there is no' flows naturally into 'you' without extra filler words.
Ладно, давайте мне тоже вот там бы накрыть.
'Alright, go ahead and set a place for me over there too.' Kostya anchors the line on 'really?!', while 'to cover' completes the thought.
'I would gladly eat something myself.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'would'. Kostya answers right away.
'Yes, right away.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'yes' before landing on 'yes'.
'Stop nodding like that.' Max anchors the line on 'in no way', while 'to nod' completes the thought.
'Take the order.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'take' and finishing on 'order'. Max answers right away.
'What is this, they want seconds now?' Max brings out the contrast between 'what' and 'this' in a few short words.
'One more salad.' The meaning hinges on 'else' working together with 'salad' in spoken Russian.
'You will get your salad.' Notice how Russian expresses 'will' and 'salad' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
А что это мы хомячим, а?
Надеюсь, не за мой счет, а?
Ладно, давайте мне тоже вот там бы накрыть.
